passage: Note from Kalyani, team manager. Ritu is warm without crowding people. When Anil's proposal was approved she was first to say, "This is brilliant, you must be so pleased!" in a bright voice, and she organised a small tea break for everyone. She thanks colleagues by name in emails. With a new colleague who seemed uneasy about hugs, she offered a namaste and moved on easily when they stepped back. She keeps jokes about work, not people. Once she caught herself gushing at a junior and asked, "Am I being too much?" The junior laughed, "No, it's nice." I have told Ritu her warmth is a real asset to the team and asked her to keep checking, as she does.

qa.a: She offers a namaste instead of hugs, keeps jokes about work, and checks whether her enthusiasm is welcome.

passage: Sunday, 11:20 pm. Zeenat, you shrieked in the kitchen tonight. Offices open on Sundays in our department, so this morning I nearly hugged Meena when she approved my leave. I stopped myself and just said thank you with my biggest smile, and she smiled back. Then tonight Dilnaz, my flatmate, got the scholarship email and I actually shrieked. I asked, "Can I hug you?" because she had looked tired all week. She said, "Yes, please, I've been waiting for someone to be loud about it." We made sooji halwa at 11 pm 🎉. I asked, "Should I tell the others?" and she said, "Family first, tomorrow you can tell whoever." I like being someone who cheers loudly for others, and I want it to be welcome every time.

qa.q: What did Zeenat and Dilnaz make at 11 pm?
qa.a: Sooji halwa.

qa.q: What was Zeenat feeling when stopping short from hugging Meena?
qa.a: Delighted about the approved leave but aware that a hug at work might not be welcome, so Zeenat chose a big smile.

qa.q: How did Zeenat make that joy welcome at home?
qa.a: Zeenat asked before hugging Dilnaz and asked before telling others.

qa.q: How might Dilnaz have felt about Zeenat's loud joy?
qa.a: Glad and supported, since she said she had been waiting for someone to be loud about it.

grounding: A young adult shares delight and affection at home by asking first, and keeps to professional limits at work.

passage: The letter came to the post office in the hill town of Almora, and Seema, who worked the counter, recognised the university seal before she'd even sorted it. It was addressed to her younger brother, Ojas. She ran it home at lunch. Ojas tore it open on the doorstep, read it twice and whispered, "I got in." Seema shrieked so loudly the neighbour's goat bolted. She wanted to throw her arms around him, but theirs wasn't a hugging family, and Ojas, at nineteen, flinched at most displays. She held her arms half out instead. "Can I?" He laughed, embarrassed, and stepped into it. Just for a second. Then he pulled back and said, "Don't tell the whole street." "Only Amma," she promised, and ran to the kitchen. Back at the post office that afternoon she kept her delight professional: a big smile for every customer, and one extra sweet in the jar for the postman.

qa.q: What did Ojas's letter tell him?
qa.a: That he had got into the university.

qa.q: How did Ojas feel about Seema's excitement?
qa.a: Ojas was happy but embarrassed, laughing, accepting a brief hug and asking her not to tell the whole street.

qa.q: How did Seema show delight in a welcome way?
qa.a: She held her arms half out and asked 'Can I?', kept the hug brief, respected his wish for privacy, and kept her joy professional at work.

qa.q: How might Amma feel hearing the news?
qa.a: Amma would likely feel proud and overjoyed at Ojas's admission.

grounding: Shows a young adult sharing delight at a sibling's success while asking before a hug, and keeping warmth professional at work.

subtype: Affectionate and delighted at work and home [Regulating]
passage: In the Seoul office, Amara found out at nine that Soo-ah's design had won the city's public signage competition. Amara wanted to do what her family in Lagos would do: shout, dance, gather everyone round and make a speech. She actually stood up. Then she remembered Soo-ah's face at her birthday last month, when the team sang loudly; she had gone bright red and stared at the floor. Warmth that embarrasses someone isn't really a gift, Amara thought. She sat back down. At lunch she slipped Soo-ah a card with a small drawing of the winning sign and one line: "I'm so proud of you. This city will read your work every day." Soo-ah read it, smiled, and put it carefully inside her notebook. "Thank you. This is perfect." Later, when the director announced the win at the team meeting, Amara clapped loudly anyway, just for three seconds. Soo-ah caught her eye and grinned.

qa.q: What did Soo-ah's design win?
qa.a: The city's public signage competition.

qa.q: How did Amara feel when she heard about the win?
qa.a: Amara felt delighted and excited, wanting to shout and dance as her family would.

qa.q: How did Amara adjust her celebration to what Soo-ah would welcome?
qa.a: She remembered Soo-ah's discomfort at loud singing and gave a private card with a drawing and a heartfelt line instead, clapping only briefly in the meeting.

qa.q: How did Soo-ah receive the card?
qa.a: Soo-ah was touched, smiling and keeping it carefully in her notebook, saying it was perfect.

grounding: Shows a young professional sharing delight at a colleague's win in a way the colleague welcomes, keeping warmth within professional limits.

passage:
In the staffroom of the primary school, Aparna saw the email over Noor's shoulder before Noor did: Noor had passed her special-education certification. Aparna's hands flew up. "Noor! You did it!"
She stopped herself mid-rush, arms half open. Noor wasn't a hugger; in two years Aparna had never seen her hug anyone at work.
"Can I hug you, or is a high five better?"
Noor laughed. "High five. And maybe tea?"
They high-fived. Then Aparna wrote on the staffroom whiteboard in big letters, "Congratulations Noor, certified!" and drew a lopsided star. Two teachers added their names. The principal stopped by and read it out at assembly.
At the tea stall later, Noor said quietly, "Nobody at home even knows yet. Thank you for making it feel real."
Aparna grinned. "You made it real. I just brought the marker."

qa.q: What certification did Noor pass?
qa.a: Her special-education certification.

qa.q: Why did Aparna stop mid-rush with arms half open?
qa.a: Aparna felt delighted but checked herself, remembering Noor wasn't a hugger and not wanting the excitement to make Noor uncomfortable. 😊

qa.q: How did Aparna show warmth while respecting limits?
qa.a: She asked "hug or high five?", went with Noor's choice, and celebrated publicly on the whiteboard so others could join in.

qa.q: What did the celebration mean to Noor?
qa.a: Noor felt seen and grateful; nobody at home knew yet, and the whiteboard and assembly made it feel real.

grounding: A young adult shares delight in a colleague's win through warm words and public celebration while checking that touch is welcome and keeping professional limits.
